The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300­0705 48 hours prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom. The City will do
it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:
Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00 p.m. the
day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will be distributed to
City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will be included in
the public comment record but not provided to City Council at the meeting.

Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted after the in­person
comments. Written Zoom comments will be read or summarized, then printed and made part
of the public record for the meeting. To participate on an item, please use the “Raise Hand”
function in Zoom and you will be called to speak at the appropriate time.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chang, Council Member Chou, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Lo, Mayor Chou

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
https://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant
to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting
agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on
duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

  THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT GRANT (CDBG) ACTION PLAN FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2025­26 AND FISCAL YEAR 2026­27
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve Resolution No. R­26­18
  adopting the revision to the Community Development Grant (CDBG) Action Plan for
  Fiscal Year 2025­26 and FY 2026­27. If City Council concurs, an appropriate motion
  would be:
  “I approve Resolution No. R­26­18 Resolution No. R­26­18 adopting the revision to
  the Community Development Grant (CDBG) Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2025­26 and
  FY 2026­27.”

  NEW BUSINESS

2.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­26­27 CERTIFYING THE JUNE 2,
  2026, ELECTION RESULTS, INCLUDING THE VOTER’S APPROVAL OF
  ORDINANCE NO. O­26­1426; ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS R­26­24
  AND R­26­25 AUTHORIZING VARIOUS AGREEMENTS WITH THE
  CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF TAX AND FEE ADMINISTRATION;
  APPROVE THE NECESSARY BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS; AND APPROVE
  AMENDMENT NO. 1 WITH HINDERLITER, DE, LLAMAS, AND
  ASSOCIATES (HDL).
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council (1) accept the official canvass
  of the Special Municipal Election held on June 2, 2026, and adopt Resolution No. R­
  26­27 declaring the results, including the voter’s approval of Ordinance No. O­26­
  1426; (2) adopt Resolution R­26­24, authorizing the City Manager to execute
  agreements with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration for
  implementation of a Local Transaction and Use Tax (3) adopt Resolution R­26­25,
  authorizing Examination of Sales or Transaction and Use Taxes Records (4) approve
  Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with Hinderliter de Llamas and Associates (HDL);
  and (5) approval of budget adjustments as indicated in the fiscal impact section. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:
  “I move to (1) accept the official canvass of the Special Municipal Election held on
  June 2, 2026, and adopt Resolution No. R­26­27 declaring the results thereof,
  including the voter’s approval of Ordinance No. O­26­1426; (2) adopt Resolution R­
  26­24; (3) adopt Resolution R­26­25; (4) approve Amendment No. 1 with Hinderliter
  de Llamas and Associates (HDL); and (5) approve the budget adjustments as
  indicated in the report.”

3.  CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­26­28 TO PLACE A
  BALLOT MEASURE ON THE NOVEMBER 3, 2026 GENERAL ELECTION
  TO RENEW THE CITY’S EXISTING UTILITY USERS TAX AS
  ORDINANCE NO. O­26­1427
  Recommendation: Staff recommend that the City Council: 1) adopt Resolution No. R­
  26­28 to place a measure on the November 3, 2026 General Election to renew the
  City’s Utility Users Tax at a rate of 6%; 2) approve Ordinance No. O­26­1427; and 3)
  approve the argument in favor of renewing the Utility Users Tax to be signed by the
  City Council or the Mayor, Vice­Mayor and members of the San Marino ballot measure
  support committee (as determined in the Mayor’s discretion). If the City Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

4.  CONSIDERATION OF REQUEST FROM SAN MARINO CITY CLUB
  CHARITABLE FUND TO INSTALL STREET LIGHT POLE BANNERS AND
  WAIVE ASSOCIATED FEES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council consider the street pole
  banner installation and fee waiver request from the San Marino City Club Charitable
  Fund. If the City Council wishes to approve the item, an appropriate motion would
  be:
  “I move to approve a request from the San Marino City Club Charitable Fund that is
  in accordance with Resolution No. R­14­22 for the installation and display of banners
  between September 15, 2026 and October 15, 2026 and waive the associated fees.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  APPROVAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH M6
  CONSULTING, INC. FOR CONTRACT BUILDING AND SAFETY
  SERVICES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council: 1) approve the Professional
  Services Agreement; 2) authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement; and
  3) approve budget adjustments needed. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:
  “I move to approve the Professional Services Agreement with m6 Consulting, Inc.,
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and authorize the necessary
  budget adjustments.”

6.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH PETER C. HARNISCH INCREASING THE
  CONTRACT AMOUNT BY $50,000, FOR A TOTAL NOT­TO­EXCEED
  AMOUNT OF $100,000, FOR CONSULTING ARBORIST SERVICES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to
  the Professional Services Agreement with Peter C. Harnisch increasing the total not­
  to­exceed amount to $100,000 for consulting arborist services and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:
  “I move to approve the Amendment No. 1 to the Professional Services Agreement
  with Peter C. Harnisch increasing the total not­to­exceed amount to $100,000 for
  consulting arborist services and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment.”

7.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MOBIUS PLANNING, LLC, INCREASING

  2029, FOR CONSULTING SERVICES RELATED TO THE STONEMAN
  HOUSING DEVELOPMENT PROJECT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 2 to
  the Professional Services Agreement with Mobius Planning, LLC, direct the City
  Attorney to prepare the amendment, and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment. If Council concurs, the appropriate motion would be:
  “I move to approve Amendment No. 2 to the Professional Services Agreement with
  Mobius Planning, LLC, increasing the not­to­exceed contract amount by $38,500 and
  extending the term of the agreement through July 12, 2029, for consulting services
  related to the evaluation of proposals received in response to the Stoneman Housing
  Development Request for Proposals and implementation of the Stoneman Housing
  Development Program; direct the City Attorney to prepare Amendment No. 2
  consistent with the scope outlined in the staff report; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute said amendment.”

8.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­26­26 APPROVING
  PARTICIPATION IN THE LOS ANGELES URBAN COUNTY PROGRAM
  FOR THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2027, THROUGH JUNE 30, 2030, AND
  AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE REQUIRED
  COOPERATION AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. R­26­
  26 approving participation in the Los Angeles Urban County Program for the period of
  July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2030, and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  required Cooperation Agreement effective July 1, 2027, with the Los Angeles County
  Development Authority (LACDA). If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:
  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R­26­26, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of San Marino, California approving participation in the Los Angeles Urban County
  Program for the period of July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2030, and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the required Cooperation Agreement effective July 1, 2027, with
  the Los Angeles County Development Authority.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
